title: Scheme and morphism conventions
statement:
This node fixes no notion of its own: it collects the conventions on schemes and morphisms of schemes used throughout, each defined in the node named. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme].

- *Quasi-compact* (the preimage of every affine open of $Y$ is quasi-compact): [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. *Quasi-separated* (the diagonal $X\to X\times_YX$ into the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] is quasi-compact): [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism].
- A scheme is *affine* if it is isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a commutative ring $A$: [def-pc-scheme], with $\operatorname{Spec}A$ as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum].
- *Separated* (the diagonal is a closed immersion), *universally closed* (every base change of $f$ is a closed map), and *proper* (separated, of finite type, and universally closed): [def-weil-proper-morphism].
- *Of finite type* (quasi-compact, and the preimage of every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $Y$ is covered by finitely many affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ a finitely generated $R$-algebra; equivalently, locally of finite type and quasi-compact): [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].
- *Of finite presentation*: locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] (Stacks Tag 01TP). The source asked only that the preimage of every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $Y$ be covered by finitely many affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ a finitely presented $R$-algebra, which is "locally of finite presentation and quasi-compact" and is weaker in general: for a field $k$, $A=k[x_1,x_2,\ldots]$, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and the non-quasi-compact open $U=\bigcup_nD(x_n)$ of $Y$, let $X$ be two copies of $Y$ glued along $U$ and $f:X\to Y$ the identity on each copy; the preimage of an affine open $V$ is covered by the two copies of $V$, but the two copies of $Y$ are affine opens of $X$ meeting in $U$, so $f$ is not quasi-separated. *Of finite presentation* always means the notion of Stacks Tag 01TP.
- *Surjective* (surjective on underlying topological spaces): [def-weil-surjective-morphism].
- *Open immersion* (identifies $X$ with an open subscheme of $Y$): [def-weil-open-immersion]. *Closed immersion* (equivalently, affine and induced on affine opens by surjective ring homomorphisms) and *immersion* (a closed immersion followed by an open immersion): [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The source added "equivalently, an open immersion followed by a closed immersion"; that is not an equivalence in general (Stacks Remark Tag 01IP, Example Tag 01QW give an immersion that does not factor so; a quasi-compact immersion does, Stacks Lemma Tag 01QV), and it is not part of this definition.
- *Finite* (affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism] with $f_*\mathcal O_X$ a finite $\mathcal O_Y$-algebra, i.e. finite ring maps over affine opens) and *integral* (affine with $f_*\mathcal O_X$ integral over $\mathcal O_Y$, i.e. integral ring maps over affine opens): [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].
- *Radicial* (for every field $K$ the map $X(K)\to Y(K)$ is injective; equivalently universally injective, or injective with purely inseparable residue field extensions): [def-weil-radicial-morphism]. *Universal homeomorphism* (every base change of $f$ is a homeomorphism of underlying spaces): [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism].
- *Flat* (every induced map of local rings $\mathcal O_{Y,f(x)}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is flat): [def-weil-flat-morphism]. *Unramified* (locally of finite type with diagonal an open immersion): [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. *Étale* (locally of finite presentation, flat and unramified): [def-weil-etale-morphism]. *Weakly étale* (flat with flat diagonal): [def-weil-weakly-etale-morphism].
- *Geometric fibre* $X_{\bar y}=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(y)}$ over a point $y\in Y$, for the residue field $\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-residue-field] and a chosen algebraic closure $\overline{\kappa(y)}$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]: [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. The source wrote it for $y\in|Y|$; where $|Y|$ means the set of closed points [def-weil-closed-points] this is the special case of closed points.
- *Geometric point* $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed: [def-weil-geometric-point].
- *Locally closed* subset (intersection of an open and a closed subset): [def-weil-locally-closed-subset]. *Constructible* subset: [def-weil-constructible-subset]. The source defined "constructible" as "a finite union of locally closed subsets"; this agrees with [def-weil-constructible-subset] on Noetherian topological spaces (Stacks Tag 005L) and differs in general (in a quasi-compact scheme a non-quasi-compact open subset is a finite union of locally closed subsets but not constructible). Constructible always means [def-weil-constructible-subset].
- A *locally closed constructible subscheme* of $Y$ is a subset $Z\subseteq Y$ that is locally closed and constructible, with a subscheme structure, i.e. an immersion $Z\to Y$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose image is $Z$.
- *Spectral* topological space (quasi-compact, quasi-separated, sober, with a basis of quasi-compact opens): [def-weil-spectral-space].

split_report.summary: The node was a grab-bag redefining some twenty-five notions. It is now a bundle of pointers, one per notion, like def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties: to the existing leaves def-pc-scheme (morphism, affine scheme), def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-finite-type-morphism (quasi-compact, finite type), def-weil-proper-morphism (separated, universally closed, proper), def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion (closed immersion, immersion), pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-weakly-etale-morphism, def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure, def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-weil-closed-points, def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-locally-closed-subset, def-weil-constructible-subset, and to eight new Mathlib leaves: def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism (QuasiSeparated), def-weil-surjective-morphism (Surjective), def-weil-finite-integral-morphism (IsFinite, IsIntegralHom), def-weil-radicial-morphism (UniversallyInjective with tfae_universallyInjective, Stacks 01S4), def-weil-universal-homeomorphism ((topologically IsHomeomorph).universally), def-weil-unramified-morphism (LocallyOfFiniteType ∧ IsOpenImmersion diagonal), def-weil-etale-morphism (Etale via Etale.iff_flat_and_formallyUnramified), def-weil-spectral-space (SpectralSpace). Corrections against Stacks, written in the statement: the source's 'finite presentation' omits quasi-separated (counterexample given; Stacks 01TP); the source's 'equivalently, an open immersion followed by a closed immersion' for immersions is false in general (Stacks 01IP, 01QW) and is dropped; 'constructible' as a finite union of locally closed subsets differs from Stacks' notion outside Noetherian spaces. The sheaf phrasing of finite/integral agrees with the affine-local definition (Mathlib's) only through Stacks 01PB; recorded in def-weil-finite-integral-morphism. Every notion now has a node and the item adds nothing of its own.

lean.note: Fixes no notion of its own (its statement says so): it collects the meanings of the scheme and morphism properties, each defined in the node it names, and fixes which variant is meant (of finite presentation = Stacks 01TP; constructible = def-weil-constructible-subset). The Mathlib facts that stand in are the matches of the named leaves: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme, QuasiCompact, QuasiSeparated, LocallyOfFiniteType, LocallyOfFinitePresentation (of finite presentation = LocallyOfFinitePresentation f ∧ QuasiCompact f ∧ QuasiSeparated f), IsSeparated, UniversallyClosed, IsProper, Surjective, IsOpenImmersion, IsClosedImmersion, IsImmersion, IsAffineHom, IsFinite, IsIntegralHom, UniversallyInjective, Flat, Etale, WeaklyEtale, Scheme.Hom.fiber, IsLocallyClosed, Topology.IsConstructible, SpectralSpace. Its one composite phrase, a locally closed constructible subscheme Z of Y, is an immersion i : Z ⟶ Y ([IsImmersion i]) with IsLocallyClosed and Topology.IsConstructible of Set.range i.base; a citer using it writes this out.
